events.title: v0.6.32 - The Multiplayer Update
events.summary: If you've tried the 9.8 demo before, this is the update to come back to.9.8 v0.6.32 - public demoMultiplayer is here. You can now host a game from the main menu and create a multiplayer universe. Hosting and joining should be simple and intuitive as it runs through Steam. Up to 4 players can share the same solar system and explore, fly and build together. events.title: v0.6.31 - major performance patch
events.summary: Directx 11 path now available for older GPUs that don't support vulkan. This should allow players that couldn't launch the game to play. Note: It'll take a long time to load the game (we're talking more than 5 minutes sometimes, if you're patient it will load)Best tier has less stalls close to QN surfaceSeveral rendering jobs spread across frames. Less hitches and slow frames overall on all tiersFixed a physics stall that could freeze the game for several seconds constantly due to an inactive cr

events.title: v0.6.29
events.summary: v0.6.29 - minor patch Linux via Proton broke on the last patch. Should be fixed so Linux players can play again.Massive improvement to medium/low graphics which should be felt especially on integrated GPUs, (measured twice FPS during rocket launches for example).Fullscreen on windows now uses borderless for fullscreen. Should fix the alt+tab multi-ghost window bug and some crashes that were occuring due to fullscreen.

events.title: v0.6.28 Update.
events.summary: v0.6.28 is live - Major performance and startup pass Demo data is starting to payoff as I can see most of the places where slowdowns, hitches and startup failures are happening. I'll keep on updating the demo to try to get the game to run as smoothly as possible in most machines. This is compounding work for the early access release later this year. events.title: 9.8 - Rocket Construction is Coming
events.summary: Hi, I'm André, solo dev behind 9.8, based in Porto, Portugal. First Steam news post for 9.8, so let me catch you up.9.8 is a 2D space agency simulator built around real orbital mechanics. You launch rockets, land on moons, deploy satellites, and expand across a handcrafted star system where every object follows the same physics.
